result:
I re-ran every acceptance check on the final tree and all of them pass. The work is still not complete: the `launch_procedure` action, the second half of §E.1, is still not built. It needs an architect's decision before it can be.

**What I found in the interrupted run's work** (WIP commit `4eee6f9`)
- Every file its handback lists exists and matches the description. The tree typechecks, so no source file was cut off.
- One stale comment in `apps/worker/src/automation/starters.ts` still pointed to `automation/request-executions.ts`; that code now lives in `platform/request-executions.ts`. I fixed the comment, which is my only code change.
- The handback's final-checks section (§9) was still an unfilled placeholder. That run's `integration.log` stops partway through, because the restart killed it during its last integration run.
- None of that run's logs counts as evidence any more. Each `-B` log is a fresh run of mine.

**Checks on the final tree** (`4eee6f9` plus my uncommitted changes)

| Check | Exit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `validate.mjs --historical --stage DG4`, at start and end | 0 / 0 | `PASS gate DG4 (historical)` |
| `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm -r build`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm openapi:lint` | 0 each | passed |
| prettier check over all files | 0 | all files formatted |
| `pnpm test`, locale unset | 0 | 1885 / 1400 / 259 passed (2 skipped by design), 0 failed |
| `pnpm test`, `C.UTF-8` | 0 | same counts |
| integration suite on a throwaway PostgreSQL (port 23800, pool 23801–23849) | 0 | 231 files, 2257 tests passed, 0 failed |

BE-J's own test files all pass: worker starters 24, API starters 9, contract 74. The pinned contract counts are unchanged, and no test failed, flaked or was retried.

**Why `launch_procedure` is still undone.** An action running as the automation's own (service) identity cannot record a procedure launch as the design stands:
- The procedure-instance table requires a real user as the launcher (`launched_by` is NOT NULL and points at a user row).
- Requesting approval for a procedure step refuses any requester who isn't a person.

I added this to the handback as §5.7, with three options for the architect:
- limit the action to rules that run as the user who triggered them;
- use the rule's owner as the launcher;
- allow an empty launcher, which needs a migration in our unused number `0077`.

I did not register the action. Registering it would make it selectable in the rule builder with nothing in the worker to run it.

**Handback:** I added a "Continuation run (T-DG5-BE-JB)" section at the top and filled in §9; earlier sections were corrected in place. It is at `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG5/T-DG5-BE-J-backend-workflow-engineer.md`, with the new logs in `T-DG5-BE-J-evidence/*-B.log`.
- No migration was added and no API endpoint beyond the interrupted run's: `GET /transformations/{id}/dependency-slips`, plus the optional `launchPlan` on `POST /transformations`.
- Run ended at 2026-10-15T00:30:24Z, about 65 minutes in, and all changes are left uncommitted.

**Still open:**
- `launch_procedure` (after the decision above).
- The "90-day tasks dated from the start date" test, which waits for BE-P.
- Starter 12, which is wrapped automatically once BE-L2 adds its handler.
- My Work needs English and Arabic text for two new message keys; the handback's §8 lists them for the front-end owner.
